identity.title: Valuation dates
identity.summary: The dates a portfolio was valued: its positions and total market value on each.

portfolios.description: Portfolio codes, as portfolio.list names them: one to a hundred, each once. Each is refused unless it is in your data scope (not_granted) and Harbour knows it (portfolio_not_found).

from.description: The first date, inclusive; the first valuation when null. A from after to is an empty window, which holds no dates.

to.description: The last date, inclusive; the latest valuation when null.

result.description: One row per portfolio and valuation date, oldest first. A portfolio valued on no date in the window contributes no rows. The data are Harbour's own, licensed from no vendor, and confidential under the firm's house rule: keep them inside the firm. Atlas reads Harbour as the gateway's own service identity and narrows every read to your data scope. An answer longer than your output limit is never cut silently: it says output_limit_exceeded. Ask for fewer portfolios or a shorter window.

items.description: A portfolio's valuation on a date.

as_of.description: The valuation date: an as_of portfolio.holdings@v1 answers for.

positions.description: The rows portfolio.holdings@v1 returns for the portfolio on this date, a position closed that day included.

market_value.description: The portfolio's total market value on the date, in its base currency: each position's market value at Harbour's rate for the date, shorts negative, summed.

loaded_at.description: When Harbour last wrote this valuation; a correction rewrites it and moves it.

errors.description: No portfolio has one of the codes asked for.
errors.next: Call portfolio.search@v1:fetch to find the code, or portfolio.list@v1:fetch for the codes you may use.

errors.description: The warehouse that serves Harbour's views is suspended or unreachable.
errors.next: Wait retry_after seconds, then repeat the call.

meaning.dates: every date the portfolio was valued between from and to, inclusive
meaning.scope: a portfolio outside the caller's data scope is refused

usage.when: You need the dates a portfolio has holdings for, before asking portfolio.holdings@v1 for one of them, or a portfolio's total value over time.
usage.when_not: You need the positions themselves: use portfolio.holdings@v1.

examples.title: The plan for a window, without running it

usage.cost: One small warehouse query, after a small read that checks each portfolio exists. explain shows the statement and runs nothing.

changelog.change: Added explain, which plans a request as fetch would and runs nothing. Added loaded_at, when Harbour last wrote each valuation. Stated the owner's choices: an empty window, the base-currency total, corrections, data handling and output limits.
